summary: Remove inert Carbon CSS rules from the reports and stock management apps
description:
Background
Two stylesheets declare Carbon class selectors without :global(). Every stylesheet in a frontend module goes through CSS Modules, so those class names are rewritten (.cds--select becomes .-esm-reports__reports__cds--select___ZsnpP), cannot match Carbon's markup, and have never had any effect.
openmrs-esm-admin-tools, packages/esm-reports-app/src/components/reports.scss lines 121-135: four width: 100% rules for .cds--date-picker, .cds--date-picker__input, .cds--select and .cds--select-input, nested under the local .formField.

openmrs-esm-stock-management, src/core/components/table/table.scss line 156: .cds--table-sort__description { display: none }.

Requested change
Delete both blocks. This is behavior-preserving, since neither rule has ever applied.
If either turns out to be wanted rather than abandoned, reinstating it changes rendering, and the correct form differs between the two:
In reports.scss, wrapping the selectors in :global() is enough. The surrounding .formField supplies the module-specific anchor.

In table.scss, :global() alone is not enough. A selector anchored only on Carbon classes is what the build guard added in openmrs/openmrs-esm-core#1869 rejects, so the rule would also need a module-owned ancestor.

The two files are in different repositories, so this needs two pull requests.
Acceptance criteria
Neither reports.scss nor table.scss contains any cds-- class name. Both files use Carbon classes only in the blocks being deleted, so a plain grep is a complete check.

Both repositories build successfully in production mode.

Existing test and lint suites pass unchanged for esm-reports-app and openmrs-esm-stock-management. No new tests are warranted: the deleted rules are inert, so there is no behavior to cover, and a clean production build is the check that no rendering depended on them.
